en: Have you heard, young fellow?
There's a killer by the name of Jack prowling
about these parts
I was sketching here by the river
and up came a body instead of a sketch!
Even I got quite a fright, I'll admit.
You once found a body around here.
And yet you keep painting here every day...
Are you not afraid of the killer?
Bah, the culprit won't bother with a shabby
old man like me.
Besides, I can't bring myself to abandon
a half-finished painting.
Have you no family?
Family, eh...
I had a wife, and children too
Fully aware how selfish it is, I wander alone
like this, painting.
You might say I left my family for my art.
An artist has to do battle with all
manner of things.
Well now, the composition's coming along.
Ah, it's you. You know, a human life
is a fleeting thing indeed.
But living is a wonderful thing.
And I'd like my dying to be wonderful too.
Don't you think so?
Well, well, so you've come.
You're the Grim Reaper, aren't you?
Now this is a surprise.
What made you think so?
Who can say? An artist's intuition, perhaps.
I sensed somehow that you were no
ordinary human.
Not quite right, I'm afraid,
but close enough.
But I have not come here
to kill you.
For a while, you shall merely be
my servant, nothing more.
I've heard that many artists have a keen
sense for such things
Perhaps this old man is a finer artist
than he appears
Oh, it's you.
Come in, come in.
I was just adding color to a painting.
You're always welcome here.
Do come by again.
Sir, what might you be doing out here,
perhaps?
Painting by the river where a body turned up
Aren't you afraid of the killer, sir?
Sir, don't you have any family?
If they knew you were painting out here,
they'd surely be terribly worried.
, my master. Your desire
note: after the name, servant mode: '{NAME}, my master. Your desire / is my desire...' (as M2#0 ', my master')

en: is my desire
I'm a sculptor of the soul.
From a single block of stone,
I can create gods and devils alike.
So, what do you think of my work?
Magnificent, isn't it?
Whoops, can't waste time chattering like this.
Rather than talk, an artist
must create.
In this world, it's easy to tell the rich
from the poor, right?
If you've got things, you're rich;
if you can barely eat, you're poor.
But it's hard to tell the good from the bad,
isn't it?
Still, live long enough, and a person's
character comes to the surface
in their face.
Hey, have you heard?
About the monstrous killer loose in
this city...
Word is, the killer's already taken a knife
note: #3920 (slice 049) should finish: 'to a whole lot of people...'
